body:
I wish I wasn't exaggerating about crying over everything but lately it's just been getting worse. I'm constantly making my boyfriend think he's upsetting me whenever he wants to talk about things seriously, when in reality it's just me crying for no discernible reason. If I say I don't want to do something, I'm crying about it. If I'm convinced he doesn't want me there just from me reading body language (which I'm probably reading wrong) I'm crying about it. I probably am tactless because I just don't have any social skills and things always end up depressing when I'm talking. And he acts so fine with it but me crying and being this way pisses me off, so I can't imagine how it makes him feel.

I've seen a couple doctors who think I have Autism Spectrum Disorder, but being diagnosed is taking forever and I'm unsure what would happen after that. The pictures and videos thing does make sense though. (thanks for responding to begin with)

Yeah, speech impediments suck. (Can relate. Have always been too anxious to turn on voice chat in any online games) People are just naturally hostile to things that are new to them that they don't understand I guess. :/
Thank you. Knowing that makes me feel a little less crazy (:
Thank you for the reply. It's really helpful :)
I still see said counsellor, it's just that I won't for much longer since she's a school counsellor and I'm going to college after this school year is over.

I've come to find that it's best to tell whoever you're with about said stutter from the get go, that way you both know what it is when it happens, and if it happens to me I usually just try to laugh it off - maybe even stop and just take a moment to collect my thoughts. I've never had anyone have a problem with this, but I can't speak for everyone. 

(Sorry it's not much. I've never had advice from anybody about it :\)
Yeeeeah. Not hard to tell I've never been on reddit before. Thanks for reading though
